claim: A cluster of four is a group and a cluster of three is not; a bird at rest has no heading, so it links to nobody.
derivation: S's four birds are 1 apart with the same heading: one cluster of 4, one group (E14).
The bird at rest has no heading, so it links to nobody although it is 1 from R's third bird. R is a cluster of 3 and the bird at rest a cluster of 1: strays. clusterCount = 1.
Seven unit headings (0, 1); the bird at rest contributes nothing. The sum is (0, 7) over 8 birds: directionalAgreement = 0.875 (E12).
Every bird's nearest neighbour is 1 away: meanNeighbourDistance = 1 (E13).
Strays: R's three birds and the bird at rest, 4 of 8, so strayShare = 0.5 (E18). One group holding half the birds reads as one group (O1).
The group is row S (x = 20 to 23, y = 20); its centre is (21.5, 20). Offsets ±0.5, ±1.5, so groupSpread = √1.25 (E19). No obstacles: birdsAtObstacles = 0 (E20).
